intro: A horn-fueled Portland band of Balkan-tinged roots rock.
story: Pancake Breakfast is Mike Midlo's Portland roots-rock troupe, a party band that can swell to nine members for tongue-in-cheek ballads, Balkan stomps and chicken-pickin' numbers, with horns and group singing. Midlo has said he chose the name because it was the happiest thing he could think of. They played Pickathon in 2009 as a fixture of the local club scene, and the band later wound down.
artist_reel_line: Mike Midlo fronted the Portland club favorite before it wound down.

intro: A North Carolina old-time string band.
story: The Freight Hoppers, a North Carolina old-time string band that grew out of a gig at the Bryson City train depot, made two Rounder albums, Where'd You Come From, Where'd You Go? in 1996 and Waiting on the Gravy Train in 1998. The Roanoke Times noted they were among the rare old-time bands making a full-time living, billing themselves as an old-time string band with overdrive. They played Pickathon in 2009, and Mile Marker came out in 2010. Founder Frank Lee has kept the band on regional stages and festival bills.
artist_reel_line: Founder Frank Lee has kept the band on regional stages and festival bills.

intro: A New York songwriter with Autumn Fallin' behind her.
story: Jaymay, the New York anti-folk songwriter Jamie Seerman, played Pickathon in 2009 with her debut, Autumn Fallin', behind her on Heavenly. A song cycle about a New York relationship ending, it struck Slant as a quintessential New York album. She went on to make independent records through 2016.
artist_reel_line: She kept releasing independent records through 2016.

intro: A rowdy Virginia string band with punk energy.
story: The Hackensaw Boys began in the fall of 1999 in Charlottesville, Virginia, when David Sickmen, Rob Bullington, Tom Peloso and Robert St. Ours turned street performing into a string band with punk-bred energy. Keep It Simple came out on Valley Entertainment around 2002 and Love What You Do on Nettwerk in 2005. They played Pickathon in 2009, after a visit in 2008. Charismo, in 2016, was their first studio album in nine years, and NPR's Scott Simon interviewed them.
artist_reel_line: Charismo, in 2016, was their first studio album in nine years.

intro: An Asheville bluegrass band with soaring female harmonies.
story: Dehlia Low, an Asheville bluegrass band known for its female harmonies and for having no banjo, formed in late 2007 out of the local jam scene. Its first two albums, the second of them Tellico in 2009, both landed in WNCW's top 20 of the year. They played Pickathon in 2009. Ravens & Crows, produced by Travis Book, came out on Rebel Records on August 2, 2011, and the band stepped back from the road in 2012. Co-founder Anya Hinkle has since built a solo career.
artist_reel_line: Co-founder Anya Hinkle went on to a solo career.

story: Mandolinist Mike Compton, a Bill Monroe-influenced player from Mississippi, and flatpicking guitarist David Grier played Pickathon in 2009 as a duo. Their Rounder album Climbing the Walls was an IBMA Album of the Year nominee, and Compton played on the O Brother, Where Art Thou? soundtrack, which won the 2002 Grammy for Album of the Year. Both still perform, and Grier was on the road with solo acoustic guitar dates in fall 2026 alongside his duo work with Compton.
artist_reel_line: David Grier toured solo in fall 2026 and still plays duo dates with Compton.

story: Town Mountain, a hard-driving Asheville bluegrass band formed in 2005 by Robert Greer and Jesse Langlais, played Pickathon in 2009, after two albums, and returned in 2010, 2016 and 2019. Leave the Bottle came out on Pinecastle in 2012, and in 2013 the IBMA named them Momentum Band of the Year, with Greer taking Vocalist of the Year. Southern Crescent charted in the top ten in 2016, and they later signed to New West, widening from bluegrass into outlaw country and Americana.
artist_reel_line: They have widened from bluegrass into outlaw country and Americana.

story: Vetiver is the San Francisco band Andy Cabic formed in 2002, and Tight Knit, its fourth album and Sub Pop debut, came out in February 2009, the year it played Pickathon. The Errant Charm followed on Sub Pop in 2011, and Complete Strangers on Easy Sound in 2015. Up on High came in 2019, and PopMatters praised it.
artist_reel_line: Up on High came out in 2019 on Mama Bird and Loose.

intro: A Brooklyn trio of ragtime and vaudeville folk.
story: The Wiyos began as a street band on Manhattan's Lower East Side, named after the 1800s Whyos gang, and later settled in Brooklyn, playing ragtime, vaudeville-folk and old-time blues. They played Pickathon in 2009 with Broken Land Bell newly out, then opened a 28-day summer tour on the Bob Dylan show. Twist followed in 2012, and the trio has toured the US and UK.

intro: A folk band honored at the Canadian Folk Music Awards.
story: Deep Dark Woods played Pickathon in 2009, the year Winter Hours won them Ensemble of the Year at the Canadian Folk Music Awards. The Place I Left Behind won Contemporary Album of the Year at the same awards in 2012, and that year the Americana Music Awards nominated them for Emerging Artist of the Year.
artist_reel_line: The Place I Left Behind won Contemporary Album of the Year in 2012.

intro: A punk-spirited Cajun band from Louisiana.
story: Lost Bayou Ramblers, the Louisiana Cajun band of brothers Andre and Louis Michot, played Pickathon in 2009 with Live: Á la Blue Moon behind them, a 2008 Grammy nominee for Best Zydeco or Cajun Music Album. They returned in 2012, the year they made music for the film Beasts of the Southern Wild, and again in 2018, the year Kalenda won the Grammy for Best Regional Roots Music Album. They toured Louisiana and Texas in fall 2026.
artist_reel_line: They toured Louisiana and Texas in fall 2026, including New Orleans's Ogden Museum.
